main_text.l: cietate fœlicissimas. Quæ ut arctius coalescerent,
diffidio opus fuisse videtur ut ex belli dispendiis pa-
cis compendia pernoscerent, eamque posthac im-
pensius colerent, perinde ut nusquam lætior dies
quam ubi tristes nebulas solis radii dispulere. Qui
vero innoxiorum ruinas improba spe præceperant,
ac ferro & flamma per summam immanitatem om-
ne concordia coalescerent, ecce rebus aliter jam flu-
entibus, quam amaram rerum vicissitudinem expe-
riuntur! ἐχθρὸν[?] illud ὥμμα[?] vivit & vigilat, justitiæ
ille oculus illibatus, hic hic est qui

page.notes: The verse stanza is set in italic and indented; its lines are run together into one paragraph. "sustulit" is read with some doubt because the long s and f are hard to tell apart at this scan resolution. The two Greek words "ἐχθρὸν" and "ὥμμα" are read from a small, faded print and are marked [?]. The catchword "EPI-" sits at the right below the last line and keeps its printed hyphen. No marginal notes are printed on this page.
